walkthroughs.body_html:
Hazardous Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Hazardous Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Hazardous Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why are composite volcanoes more explosive than shield volcanoes?
options: Because composite volcanoes are found in cold climates.
Composite volcanoes have high-silica, viscous magma that traps gas, causing pressure to build until violent eruption; shield volcanoes have runny basaltic lava that releases gas easily.
Because composite volcanoes are taller and have more lava.
El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between hard and soft engineering for flood management?
options: Hard engineering always works better than soft engineering at preventing floods.
Because composite volcanoes are found in cold climates.
Soft engineering means using softer materials like sand instead of concrete.
Hard engineering uses built structures (dams, levees, channelisation) to control flow; soft engineering works with natural processes (afforestation, wetland restoration, floodplain zoning).

mcqs.q: What happens during an El Nino event?
options: El Nino is when the ocean gets colder near Peru.
Soft engineering means using softer materials like sand instead of concrete.
El Nino is the name of a specific hurricane that hit Mexico.
Trade winds weaken, warm water that normally pools in the western Pacific spreads east, disrupting weather patterns globally — drought in Australia, floods in South America.
